verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              ततो विनशनं राजञ्जगामाथ हलायुधः। शूद्राभीरान्प्रतिद्वेषाद्यत्र नष्टा सरस्वती॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said "Then Baladeva, O king, went to Vinashana where the Sarasvati has disappeared out of view in consequence of her hatred for Shudras and Abhiras.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मात्तु ऋषयो नित्यं प्राहुर्विनशनेति च। तत्राप्युपस्पृश्य बलः सरस्वत्यां महाबलः॥२॥
verses.english: And because the Sarasvati, on account of this contempt, is lost there Rishis, O chief of the Bharatas, always name the place as Vinashana.

verses.sanskrit: सुभूमिकं ततोऽगच्छत्सरस्वत्यास्तटे वरे। तत्र चाप्सरसः शुभ्रा नित्यकालमतन्द्रिताः॥३॥
verses.english: Having bathed in that tirtha of the Sarasvati, the powerful Baladeva then went to Subhumika situate on the excellent bank of the same river.

verses.sanskrit: क्रीडाभिर्विमलाभिश्च क्रीडन्ति विमलाननाः। तत्र देवाः सगन्धर्वा मासि मासि जनेश्वर॥४॥
verses.english: There many fair-complexioned and beautiful-faced. Apsaras are always engaged in innocent pastimes.

verses.sanskrit: अभिगच्छन्ति तत्तीर्थं पुण्यं ब्राह्मणसेवितम्। तत्रादृश्यन्त गन्धर्वास्तथैवाप्सरसां गणाः॥५॥
verses.english: The celestials and the Gandharvas, every month, O king, go to that sacred shrine which is the resort of Brahman himself.

verses.sanskrit: समेत्य सहिता राजन्यथाप्राप्तं यथासुखम्। तत्र मोदन्ति देवाश्च पितरश्च सवीस्थः॥६॥
verses.english: The Gandharvas and various clans of Apsaras are to be seen there, O king, passing their days happily.

verses.sanskrit: पुण्यैः पुष्पैः सदा दिव्यैः कीर्यमाणाः पुनः पुनः। आक्रीडभूमिः सा राजंस्तासामप्सरसां शुभा॥७॥
verses.english: There the celestials and departed manes in the midst of the showers of sacred and auspicious flowers sport in joy.

verses.sanskrit: सुभूमिकेति विख्याता सरस्वत्यास्तटे वरे। तत्र स्नात्वा च दत्त्वा च वसु विप्राय माधवः॥८॥
verses.english: There all the creepers are covered with flowers. And because, O king, that spot is the beautiful sporting ground of those Apsaras, therefore is that shrine on the charming bank of the Sarasvati is called Subhumika.

verses.sanskrit: श्रुत्वा गीतं च तद्दिव्यं वादित्राणां च निःस्वनम्। छायाश्च विपुला दृष्ट्वा देवगन्धर्वरक्षसाम्॥९॥
verses.english: Baladeva of Madhu's race, having bathed in that tirtha and distributed immense riches amongst the Brahmanas, heard the sound of those celestial songs and musical instruments.

verses.sanskrit: गन्धर्वाणां ततस्तीर्थमागच्छद्रोहिणीसुतः। विश्वावसुमुखास्तत्र गन्धर्वास्तपसान्विताः॥१०॥
verses.english: He also saw there many shadows of gods, Gandharvas and Rakshasas. The son of Rohini then proceeded to the tirtha of the Gandharvas.

verses.sanskrit: नृत्यवादित्रगीतं च कुर्वन्ति सुमनोरमम्। तत्र दत्त्वा हलधरो विप्रेभ्यो विविधं वसु॥११॥
verses.english: There many Gandharvas, headed by Vishvavasu and possessed of ascetic merit, pass their time in dance and singing many sweet songs.

verses.sanskrit: अजाविकं गोखरोष्ट्रं सुवर्णं रजतं तथा। भोजयित्वा द्विजान्कामैः सन्तर्प्य च महाधनैः॥१२॥
verses.english: Giving away various kinds of riches to the Brahmanas, as also goat and sheep and kine and mules and camels and gold and silver.

verses.sanskrit: प्रययौ सहितो विप्रैः स्तूयमानश्च माधवः। तस्माद्गन्धर्वतीर्थाच्च महाबाहुररिन्दमः॥१३॥
verses.english: And feeding many Brahmanas and satisfying them with many rich gifts as desired by them, Baladeva, of Madhu's race, left that place accompanied by many Brahmanas and praised by them.

verses.sanskrit: गर्गस्रोतो महातीर्थमाजगामैककुण्डली। तत्र गर्गेण वृद्धेन तपसा भावितात्मना॥१४॥
verses.english: Leaving that tirtha the favourite haunt of the Gandharvas, that mighty-armed chastiser of foes, having but one ear-ring, then went to the famous tirtha called Gargashrota.

verses.sanskrit: कालज्ञानगतिश्चैव ज्योतिषां च व्यतिक्रमः। उत्पाता दारुणाश्चैव शुभाश्च जनमेजय॥१५॥
verses.english: There, in that sacred tirtha of the Sarasvati, the illustrious and old Garga, having a soul cleansed by ascetic penances, O Janamejaya, had mastered the knowledge of time and its course, of the deviations of luminous bodies (in the sky) and of all auspicious and inauspicious portents.

verses.sanskrit: सरस्वत्या शुभे तीर्थे विदिता वै महात्मना। तस्य नाम्ना च तत्तीर्थं गर्गस्रोत इति स्मृतम्॥१६॥
तत्र गर्गं महाभागमृषयः सुव्रता नृप। उपासाञ्चक्रिरे नित्यं कालज्ञानं प्रति प्रभो॥१७॥
तत्र गत्वा महाराज बलः श्वेतानुलेपनः। विधिवद्धि धनं दत्वा मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम्॥१८॥
verses.english: Besmeared with white sandal-paste O king, Baladeva, going to that tirtha, duly distributed wealth amongst many ascetics of pure souls.

verses.sanskrit: उच्चावचांस्तथा भक्ष्यान्विप्रेभ्यो विप्रदाय सः। नीलवासास्तदागच्छच्छङ्खतीर्थं महायशाः॥१९॥
verses.english: Having distributed also many sorts of rich food amongst the Brahmanas, that illustrious one, clad in blue robes, then went to the tirtha called Shankha.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रापश्यन्महाशङ्खं महामेरुमिवोच्छ्रितम्। श्वेतपर्वतसङ्काशमृषिसन्धैर्निषेवितम्॥२०॥
verses.english: There, on the bank of the Sarasvati that powerful palmyra-emblemed hero beheld a gigantic tree called Mahashankha, tall as Meru, looking like the white-mountain and resorted to by many Rishis.

verses.sanskrit: सरस्वत्यास्तटे जातं नगं तालध्वजो बली। यक्षा विद्याधराश्चैव राक्षसाश्चामितौजसः॥२१॥
verses.english: There dwell Yakshas and Vidyadharas and Rakshasas of great energy and Pishachas of incomparable might and Siddhas, in thousands.

verses.sanskrit: पिशाचाश्वामितबला यत्र सिद्धाः सहस्रशः। ते सर्वे ह्यशनं त्यक्त्वा फलं तस्य वनस्पतेः॥२२॥
verses.english: Desisting from other kinds of food, all of them observe vows and regulations and take at the proper time the fruits of that king of the forest for their sustenance and rove separately unseen by men, O foremost of men. That monarch of the forest, O king, is celebrated throughout the world.

verses.sanskrit: व्रतैश्च नियमैश्चैव काले काले स्म भुञ्जते। प्राप्तैश्च नियमैस्तैस्तैर्विचरन्तः पृथक् पृथक्॥२३॥
अदृश्यमाना मनुजैर्व्यचरन्पुरुषर्षभ। एवं ख्यातो नरव्याघ्र लोकेऽस्मिन्स वनस्पतिः॥२४॥
ततस्तीर्थं सरस्वत्याः पावनं लोकविश्रुतम्। तस्मिंश्च यदुशार्दूलो दत्वा तीर्थे पयस्विनीः॥२५॥
verses.english: That tree is the cause of this tirtha. Having given away many milch cows, vessels of copper and iron and diverse sorts of other vessels, that foremost Yadu's race, viz., Baladeva, having the plough for his weapon, worshipped the Brahmanas and was adored by them in return. He then, O king, went to the Dvaita lake.

verses.sanskrit: ताम्रायसानि भाण्डानि वस्त्राणि विविधानि च। पूजयित्वा द्विजांश्चैव पूजितश्च तपोधनैः॥२६॥
पुण्यं द्वैतवनं राजन्नाजगाम हलायुधः। तत्र गत्वा मुनीन् दृष्ट्वा नानावेषधरान्बलः॥२७॥
verses.english: Arrived there, Vala saw various ascetics dressed diversely. Bathing in its waters, he adored the Brahmanas.

verses.sanskrit: आप्लुत्य सलिले चापि पूजयामास वै द्विजान्। तथैव दत्त्वा विप्रेभ्यः परिभोगान् सुपुष्कलान्॥२८॥
verses.english: Having distributed profusely amongst the Brahmanas various articles of enjoyment Baladeva then, O king, went on along the southern bank of the Sarasvati.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रायाद्बलो राजन् दक्षिणेन सरस्वतीम्। गत्वा चैवं महाबाहुर्नातिदूरे महायशाः॥२९॥
धर्मात्मा नागधन्वानं तीर्थमागमदच्युतः। यत्र पन्नगराजस्य वासुकेः सन्निवेशनम्॥३०॥
verses.english: The mighty-armed and illustrious Rama, of pure soul and unmitigated glory, then proceeded to the tirtha called Nagadhanvana.

verses.sanskrit: महाद्युतेर्महाराज बहुभिः पन्नगैर्वृतम्। ऋषीणां हि सहस्राणि यत्र नित्यं चतुर्दश॥३१॥
verses.english: Abounding with snakes, O king, it was the abode of the highly effulgent Vasuki, the king of serpents. There four and then ten thousand Rishis also lived permanently.

verses.sanskrit: यत्र देवाः समागम्य वासुकिं पन्नगोत्तमम्। सर्वपन्नगराजानमभ्यषिञ्चन् यथाविधि॥३२॥
verses.english: Having come there in days of yore the celestials had, according to due rites, installed the great snake Vasuki as king of all the snakes. There is no fear of snakes in that place Oyou of Kuru's race.

verses.sanskrit: पन्नगेभ्यो भयं तत्र विद्यते न स्म पौरव। तत्रापि विधिवद्दत्वा विप्रेभ्यो रत्नसञ्चयान्॥३३॥
प्रायात्प्राचीं दिशं तत्र तत्र तीर्थान्यनेकशः। सहस्रशतसङ्ख्यानि प्रथितानि पदे पदे॥३४॥
verses.english: Duly distributing many valuable articles there amongst the Brahmanas Baladeva then set out with face towards the east and reached, one after another, hundreds and thousands of celebrated tirthas situated all around.

verses.sanskrit: आप्लुत्य तत्र तीर्थेषु यथोक्तं तत्र चर्षिभिः। कृत्वोपवासनियमं दत्त्वा दानानि सर्वशः॥३५॥
verses.english: Bathing in all those tirthas and observing fasts and other vows as sanctioned by the Rishis and given away immense riches and saluting all the ascetics who lived there, Baladeva once more set out, along the way pointed out to him by those ascetics for reaching that spot where the Sarasvati turns in an eastward direction like torrents of rain bent by the velocity of the storm. The river took that course for seeing the great Rishis dwelling in the forest of Naimisha.

verses.sanskrit: अभिवाद्य मुनींस्तान्वै तत्र तीर्थनिवासिनः। उद्दिष्टमार्गः प्रययौ यत्र भूयः सरस्वती॥३६॥
प्राङ्मुखं वै निववृते वृष्टिर्वातहता यथा। ऋषीणां नैमिषयाणामवेक्षार्थं महात्मनाम्॥३७॥
निवृत्तां तां सरिच्छ्रेष्टां तत्र दृष्ट्वा तु लाङ्गली। बभूव विस्मितो राजन् बलः श्वेतानुलेपनः॥३८॥

जनमेजय उवाच।
              कस्मात्सरस्वती ब्रह्मन्निवृत्ता प्राङ्मुखीभवत्। व्याख्यातमेतदिच्छामि सर्वमध्वर्युसत्तम॥३९॥
verses.english: Janamejaya said "Why O Brahmana, did the Sarasvati bend her course there towards the east. O best of Adhvaryus, you should tell me everything regarding this.

verses.sanskrit: कस्मिंश्चित्कारणे तत्र विस्मितो यदुनन्दनः। निवृत्ता हेतुना केन कथमेव सरिद्वरा॥४०॥
verses.english: Why was that delighter of the Yadus filled with wonder? Why, indeed did that best of rivers thus change her course."

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              पूर्वं कृतयुगे राजन्नैमिषेयास्तपस्विनः। वर्तमाने सुविपुले सत्रे द्वादशवार्षिके॥४१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said "Formerly, in the Satya Yuga, O king, the ascetics living in Naimisha were engaged in a great sacrifice extending for twelve years.

verses.sanskrit: ऋषयो बहवो राजंस्तत्सत्रमभिपेदिरे। उषित्वा च महाभागास्तस्मिन्सत्रे यथाविधि॥४२॥
verses.english: Many Rishis, O king, came to that sacrifice. Passing their time according to proper rites, in the celebration of that sacrifice, those great Rishis, after the termination of that twelve year's sacrifice at Naimisha, set out in large numbers for seeing the various sacred shrines.

verses.sanskrit: निवृत्ते नैमिषेये वै सत्रे द्वादशवार्षिके। आजग्मुर्ऋषयस्तत्र बहवस्तीर्थकारणात्॥४३॥
ऋषीणां बहुलत्वात्तु सरस्वत्या विशाम्पते। तीर्थानि नगरायन्ते कूले वै दक्षिणे तदा॥४४॥
verses.english: On account of the number of the Rishis, O king, the tirthas on the southern banks of the Sarasvati all looked like towns and cities.

verses.sanskrit: समन्तपञ्चकं यावत्तावत्ते द्विजसत्तमाः। तीर्थलोभान्नरव्याघ्र नद्यास्तीरं समाश्रिताः॥४५॥
verses.english: Those foremost of Brahmanas, O foremost of men, being anxious to enjoy the merits of tirthas, took up thcir abodes on the bank of the river up to Samantapanchaka.

verses.sanskrit: जुह्वतां तत्र तेषां तु मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम्। स्वाध्यायेनातिमहता बभूवुः पूरिता दिशः॥४६॥
verses.english: The whole region was as if filled with loud Vedic recitations of those Rishis of pure souls, all engaged in pouring libations of sacrificial fires.

verses.sanskrit: अग्निहोत्रैस्ततस्तेषां क्रियमाणैर्महात्मनाम्। अशोभत सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा दीप्यमानैः समन्ततः॥४७॥
वालखिल्या महाराज अश्मकुट्टाश्च तापसाः। दन्तोलूखलिनश्चान्ये प्रसङ्ख्यानास्तथा परे॥४८॥
वायुभक्षा जलाहाराः पर्णभक्षाश्च तापसाः। नानानियमयुक्ताश्च तथा स्थण्डिलशायिनः॥४९॥
verses.english: Valakhilyas and Ashmarkuttas, Dantolukhalinas, Samprakshyanas and other ascetics, as also those living on air and those living on water and those living on dry leaves of trees and various others who practised diverse kinds of vows and those that lived on bare and hard earth, all came to that spot in the vicinity of the Sarasvati. And they rendered that foremost of rivers highly beautiful like the celestials beautifying with their presence the heavenly rivers called Mandakini.

verses.sanskrit: आसन्वै मुनयस्तत्र सरस्वत्याः समीपतः। शोभयन्तः सरिच्छ्रेष्ठां गङ्गामिव दिवौकसः॥५०॥
शतशश्च समापेतुर्ऋषयः सत्रयाजिनः। तेऽवकाशं न ददृशुः सरस्वत्या महाव्रताः॥५१॥
verses.english: Hundreds of Rishis, all given to the observance of sacrifices, came there. Those observers of great vows could not find sufficient accommodation on the banks of the Sarasvati.

verses.sanskrit: ततो यज्ञोपवीतैस्ते तत्तीर्थं निर्मिमाय वै। जुहुवुश्चाग्निहोत्रांश्च चक्रुश्च विविधाः क्रियाः॥५२॥
verses.english: Measuring small plots of land with their sacred threads, they celebrated Agnihotras and other rites.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तमृषिसङ्घातं निराशं चिन्तयान्वितम्। दर्शयामास राजेन्द्र तेषामर्थे सरस्वती॥५३॥
verses.english: The river Sarasvati saw, O king, those Rishis filled with despair and anxiety for want of a commodious tirtha wherein to perform their rites.
verses.bhavadeepa: यज्ञोपवीतैः यज्ञसूत्रैः। तीर्थं त्रेताग्नीनामुत्तरभागं तीर्थत्वेन श्रौते प्रसिद्धं निर्मिमाय निर्मायेत्यर्थः॥५२॥

verses.sanskrit: ततः कुञ्जान् बहून्कृत्वा सन्निवृत्ता सरस्वती। ऋषीणां पुण्यतपसां कारुण्याजनमेजय॥५४॥
verses.english: Accordingly that best of streams came there, having made sufficient accommodation on her bank for those Rishis, out of compassion for them, O Janamejaya.

verses.sanskrit: ततो निवृत्य राजेन्द्र तेषामर्थे सरस्वती। भूयः प्रतीच्यभिमुखी प्रसुस्राव सरिद्वरा॥५५॥
verses.english: Having thus, O king, changed her course for their sake, the Sarasvati, that best of rivers, once more flowed in a westerly direction, to make the arrival of the Rishis there successful. O king, the great river accomplished there this wonderful feat.

verses.sanskrit: अमोघा गमनं कृत्वा तेषां भूयो व्रजाम्यहम्। इत्युद्भुतं महच्चक्रे तदा राजन्महानदी॥५६॥
एवं स कुञ्जो राजन्वै नैमिषीय इति स्मृतः। कुरुश्रेष्ठ कुरुक्षेत्रे कुरुष्व महतीं क्रियाम्॥५७॥
verses.english: Thus those reservoirs of water, O king, where formed in Naimisha. There, Kurukshetra, O Kuru chief, do you celebrate grand sacrifices and rites. Beholding those innumerable reservoirs of water and seeing that best of rivers change her course, the highsouled Rama was filled with wonder.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र कुञ्जान्बहून् दृष्ट्वा निवृत्तां च सरस्वतीम्। बभूव विस्मयस्तत्र रामस्याथ महात्मनः॥५८॥
उपस्पृश्य तु तत्रापि विधिवद्यदुनन्दनः। दत्त्वा दायान् द्विजातिभ्यो भाण्डानि विविधानि च॥५९॥
भक्ष्यं भोज्यं च विविधं ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रदाय च। ततः प्रायाद्बलो राजन्पूज्यमानो द्विजातिभिः॥६०॥
verses.english: Bathing in those tirthas duly and distributing wealth and various other articles of enjoyment ainongst the Brahmanas, that delighter of Yadu's race also gave away various kinds of food and desirable articles to them. Adored by those Rishis, Vala, O king, left that foremost of all tirthas on the Sarasvati, at (viz., Sapta-Sarasvat). Numerous birds also lived there. And it abounded with Vadari, Inguda, Kacmaryya, Plahsha, Ashvattha, Vibhitaka, Kakkola, Palasha, Karira, Pilu and various other kinds of trees that grow on the banks of the Sarasvati.

verses.sanskrit: सरस्वतीतीर्थवरं नानाद्विजगणायुतम्। बदरेङ्गु्दकाश्मर्यप्लक्षाश्वत्थबिभीतकैः॥६१॥
कङ्कोलैश्च पलाशैश्च करीरैः पीलुभिस्तथा। सरस्वतीतीर्थरुहैस्तरुभिर्विविधैस्तथा॥६२॥
करूषकवरैश्चैव बिल्वैराम्रातकैस्तथा। अतिमुक्तकषण्डैश्च पारिजातैश्च शोभितम्॥६३॥
verses.english: And it was adorned with forests of Karushakas, Vilvas Vilvas and Amratakas and Atimuktas and Kashandas and Parijatas.

verses.sanskrit: कदलीवनभूयिष्ठं दृष्टिकान्तं मनोहरम्। वाय्वम्बुफलपर्णादैर्दन्तोलूखलिकैरपि॥६४॥
verses.english: It abounded with forests of Plantains pleasant to view and most charming. And it was haunted by various ascetics, some living on air, some water, some on fruits, some on leaves, some on raw raise again which they husked with the aid only of stones and some that were called Vaneyas. And it was filled with the chauntings of the Vedas and abounded with diverse kinds of animals.

verses.sanskrit: तथाश्मकुट्टैर्वानेयैर्मुनिभिर्बहुभिर्वृतम्। स्वाध्यायघोषसङ्घुष्टं मृगयूथशताकुलम्॥६५॥
अहिंस्रैर्धर्मपरमैर्नृभिपत्यर्थसेवितम्। सप्तसारस्वतं तीर्थमाजगाम हलायुधः। यत्र मकुणकः सिद्धस्तपस्तेपे महामुनिः॥६६॥
